editorial:
You follow Leo San Juan and his brother Nando as a simple trip home turns into a rescue mission after the Black Charro tricks Leo and pulls an innocent girl into the underworld. The movie mixes spooky Mexican folklore with bright animation, quick jokes, and family-friendly scares, so you get adventure without feeling too heavy. Leo’s friends join the chase, giving the story a warm team spirit and plenty of chatter along the way. It feels like a road trip that suddenly becomes a ghost story, but it stays friendly enough for younger viewers.

The action moves fast, the underworld scenes look colorful, and the voice work keeps characters lively. Some jokes land better than others, and the plot can feel busy, but the heart stays clear. If you enjoy animated fantasy with folklore flavor, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for family movie night. It is best when you want something energetic and not too dark.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Leo confronts the Black Charro in the underworld and works with his friends to rescue the innocent girl. The twist is that the Charro did not just want another soul; he chose Leo for a deeper reason tied to Leo himself. Leo outsmarts him, breaks the hold on the girl, and the group escapes back to the living world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated folklore adventures with family-friendly scares.
